decisions.quote:
Results showed direct effects of reinforcement over IBC3
and indirect effects over R1. Two effects were observed
in IBC3. If, as in Vichi et al (2009) and Lopes (2010),
the study considers only if successive gains reached the
criterion for contingency change, then we can state that
the data here obtained replicated the ones from Vichi et
al. and disagree with the ones from Lopes, since all groups
reached these criteria. In this sense, the contingencies here
manipulated established control over collective behaviors,
being an experimental analogous to metacontingencies.

Revista Latinoamericana de Psicología

Volumen 44

No 1

However, the statistical analysis did not confirm
the establishment of control by Contingency A, only
by contingency B. Since Vichi et al. (2009) and Lopes
(2010) did not conduct such statistical treatment, the
comparison cannot be made. This data suggests that
this procedure needs to be refined in order to obtain
reliable analogous of metacontingencies with all the
implemented contingencies. Since it is a group design, this
decisions.reason: In Vichi, Andery, & Glenn (2009), two four-person groups showed chip-division patterns (IBC3) controlled by both alternating Contingencies A (equal division) and B (unequal division). Testing 25 participants across three larger groups (G1, G2, G3) over six sessions with accumulated chips, the authors state conditionally that if one considers only reaching the successive-gains criterion for contingency change, all three groups met the criteria and replicated Vichi et al. (2009). However, they immediately qualify this synthesis: visual inspection showed G2 ended session exposure without establishing controlling relations under Contingency B, and binomial Z-tests confirmed above-chance correct divisions in both contingencies only for G1 (A: 60.4%, p=0.019; B: 67.7%, p=0.002), whereas G2 and G3 showed significant control only under Contingency B (p=0.007 and p=0.002) and failed to reach significance overall or under Contingency A. Because the authors explicitly conclude that their group design demands statistically significant differences, that statistical analysis failed to confirm control under Contingency A across groups, and that the procedure requires refinement to obtain reliable metacontingency analogues across all implemented contingencies, the replication outcome is mixed.

scope_review.parent_objection: The first reply codes mixed from within-study significance differences between Contingencies A/B. Discussion says the original studies did not conduct that statistical treatment, so the comparison cannot be made. On the original criterion, all groups replicate Vichi. Resolve whether Rule 1 overall/focal successful, mixed, or methodological-flaw special verdict is supported. Do not substitute our own p-value assessment or comparison of a new statistical analysis for the original test. Read entire Discussion including critique and originals comparison. Retain genuinely unresolved if needed.

prior_reply.quote: The visual inspections which supported these analyses are not fully confirmed statistically. Considering that only two possible dividing responses were permitted (equal or unequal), the verification of contingency control over these responses depends on the confirmation that the correct responses proportion was above 50%. In G1, the total proportion of correct divisions after each winning round was 63.4% (Z=2.43; p=0.008). This higher proportion was confirmed in both contingencies (Contingency A: 60.4%, Z=2.07 p=0.019; Contingency B: 67.7%, Z= 2.89 p=0.002). In G2 and G3 the proportion of “+” signs subsequent to winnings was 58.0% and 55.1% respectively, but they were not statistically superior to 50% considering α=0.05 (G2: Z=1.44, p=0.074; G3: Z=0.91, p=0.182). Controlling relations of earnings over division responses were confirmed for both G2 and G3 under contingency B (G2: Z=2.42, p=0.007 and G3: Z=2.92, p=0.002). However, statistical significance was not reached when they were under contingency A.
prior_reply.reason: Although all groups reached the contingency-change criterion as in Vichi et al. (2009), the authors qualify that visual inspection was not fully confirmed statistically: controlling relations were statistically significant across both contingencies in only one group (G1), whereas in the other two groups (G2 and G3) control was confirmed only under Contingency B and not Contingency A.
